methods.name: Morningstar Expected Return Framework
methods.description: Top-down asset-class model that blends current valuations, macro assumptions and mean-reversion to produce long-term real return forecasts. Morningstar uses it to rank relative opportunities such as South African diversified miners versus precious-metal producers.
methods.evidence: “Through the lens of Morningstar’s expected return framework, South African Resources currently ranks quite low …”

methods.name: Wealth Forecasting Engine & Private-Market Simulation
methods.description: A stochastic simulation toolkit that injects PitchBook private-market indices into target-date glide paths. Scenarios with a 5–10 % private-asset sleeve are run to measure changes in median lifetime returns, volatility and liquidity.
methods.evidence: “Preliminary simulations from Morningstar’s Wealth Forecasting Engine … suggest that adding 5%–10% diversified private exposure to target-date glide paths can raise median lifetime returns by 20–40 basis points annually.”

methods.name: Valuation-Implied Return Model for Risk Profiles
methods.description: Forward-looking real-return estimates are derived from asset-class valuations and mapped to multi-asset risk profiles (All-Growth, Balanced, Conservative, etc.) to stress-test sequencing risk in retirement plans.
methods.evidence: Chart: “Forecast 10-Year Annual Real Return by Risk Profile as of Sept. 30, 2025.”

methods.name: Behaviour-Aware Rebalancing Playbook
methods.description: Rule-based process that combines automatic rebalancing, counter-cyclical trades and client education to curb behavioural mistakes during volatility and keep portfolios aligned with long-term targets.
methods.evidence: “Morningstar’s investment team follows this approach: … Rebalance portfolios back to target allocations … Seek opportunities where markets have over-corrected relative to fundamentals …”
